text.aria-label: Title text 'Stations: December 2022 to December 2025, 60,033 site-hours'
Title text 'Figure 1: CAMS has the lowest error of the gridded products tested on each of the four row sets'
text.tspan: Figure 1: CAMS has the lowest error of the gridded products tested on
each of the four row sets

text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Each product's own mean absolute error, sorted best first within its block. Compare products only within a block: each block is scored on its own rows, so an error in one block is not comparable with an error in another. Overlapping intervals do not make two products equal: the intervals are wide mainly because every product's error swings together from month to month, a swing that Figure 2's paired contrasts cancel. ECMWF ENS is a forecast 5 to 20 hours ahead from a 00 UTC run; ERA5's radiation is 1 to 12 hours ahead. The station rows rest on one pyranometer: all six generators take the same nearest radiation station, 17 to 31 km away. Rows marked (post hoc) were added after the first run: two ways of rebuilding UKV's hourly value from its snapshots. Dot: estimate. Line: 95% interval from resampling whole months. Capacity is each generator's 99th-percentile output. Six solar farms in Lincolnshire. Lighter, hollow rows are CAMS and ERA5, repeated in every block as a yardstick and scored on that block's own rows.'
